snippet.description:

Frank’s RedHot Sharp Cheddar Chicken Macaroni

Makes 8 meal-prep containers

Shopping List

* 4 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast
* 2 boxes Carb Diem elbow pasta
* 2 (8 oz) blocks Kerrygold sharp cheddar cheese
* 1 (8 oz) block 1/3-less-fat cream cheese
* ½ cup Fairlife fat-free milk
* ¼ cup Frank’s RedHot Original Sauce

Instructions

1. Add 4 lb chicken breast to your skillet and cook until it reaches an internal temperature of 165°F.
    * 16g salt
    * 8g black pepper
    * 12g garlic powder
    * 12g onion powder

2. Cook both boxes of Carb Diem elbow pasta according to the package instructions. Drain the pasta when finished.

3. Add the cooked pasta back to the skillet. Add:
    * ½ cup Fairlife fat-free milk
    * 8 oz 1/3-less-fat cream cheese
    * 2 (8 oz) blocks Kerrygold sharp cheddar cheese
    * ¼ cup Frank’s RedHot Original Sauce

4. Mix everything together until the cream cheese and sharp cheddar are completely melted and the pasta is evenly coated.

5. While the cheese is melting, slice the cooked chicken breast into strips.

6. Divide the pasta evenly between 8 meal-prep containers, laying down a blanket of pasta first.

7. Lay the sliced chicken breast over the pasta.

Storage and Reheating

* Keep 4 containers refrigerated and freeze the remaining 4.

* From the refrigerator: Add ¼ cup water and microwave for 1 minute 30 seconds to 2 minutes.

* From frozen: Add ¼ cup water and microwave for 5 minutes 30 seconds.

snippet.title: How a 0.2Hz Wave Took Down Two Countries’ Power Grids
snippet.description:
🔌 How did a slow 0.2Hz wave trigger one of Europe’s biggest blackouts? On April 28, 2025, the Iberian power grid—spanning Spain and Portugal—collapsed in under 90 seconds. In this video, I explain exactly what went wrong, why it wasn’t a “renewables problem,” and how it could happen again.

As a grid engineer, I break down:

- The five cascading phases of the blackout
- Why low demand and excess reactive power primed the system for failure
- What inter-area oscillations are (and why they’re so dangerous)
- How protection relays and poor ride-through settings accelerated collapse
- What went wrong with voltage control and shared infrastructure
- The roles of France, Morocco, and Portugal in restarting the grid
- What this means for the future of high-renewables grids like the UK

Spoiler: Renewables weren't the root cause, but poor integration and weak grid planning were.

📈 Whether you're an energy nerd, an engineer, or just curious how a wave can take down two countries' power, this video dives deep with expert insight and real data from official blackout reports by ENTSO-E, REE, and AELEC.

0:00 Intro
1:12 Phase Zero, Why
5:35 Phase 1, Inter-Area Oscillations
10:30 Overvoltage Protection and Ride Through
12:00 SCADA
12:40 RoCoF & Callide C4

15: 20 Transformer Taps

27:05 Out-Takes

Corrections:
1:49 Heaters are a resistive load, not reactive generally.
15:35 I wrongly point at the LV side. Tap changers are typically on the HV side (taller side) however either side can be the primary or secondary depending on context. In a step up transformer the LV side would be primary.

HOW TO DO THIS: Download the Too good to go app to see what options are available in your area. The concept of Too good to go is to reduce food waste so most of the items will be at their sell by date and potentially after. If this bothers you please do not use this app. 
If you click the store that you’re wanting to get a bag from and they are not available it should tell you the time to check back for when they upload the next bags. If you look at your map and there’s nothing there, make sure to filter for sold out to show the bags that are not currently available. As they mention in the descriptions on the app, variety is not guaranteed. What they put in the bag is what they have left over that night so there is a chance that you will get multiples of stuff. If you are a picky eater, this is not for you. Whole Foods specifically values their bags at the original price. Don’t get one and expect to get fresh food and a wide variety. You can only pick up in the time that it is listed for pick up if you come before or after you cannot get the bag. One again: YOU CANNOT CHOOSE WHAT IS IN THE BAG...
Make sure to pay attention to ratings if there’s anything under a 4.5 or even a 4 star maybe don’t go to that one especially if you’re prone to complaining. Moral of the story don’t be upset if you don’t get exactly what you want and it’s stuff you don’t like. If you’re that picky just go to a restaurant. #toogoodtogo #haul #food

In this video, we show the real-life process of building a secret modern two-story treehouse deep in the jungle, completely by hand — no machines, no power tools, only pure primitive skills and teamwork. Over 69 days, two men worked from sunrise to sunset to create this amazing treehouse made entirely from natural materials found in the forest.

🌿 Step-by-Step Construction Journey:

Day 1–5: We searched for the perfect tree in a safe and strong jungle area. Once chosen, we cleared the ground and prepared bamboo, vines, and clay for the foundation.

Day 6–15: The base pillars and support beams were built using thick bamboo tied together with jungle rope. This strong structure formed the foundation for two floors.

Day 16–25: The first floor was built with split bamboo planks and clay sealing to make it waterproof. Walls were added using woven bamboo panels for strength and privacy.

Day 26–35: The second floor began to take shape with additional bamboo frames. We carefully balanced the weight between branches for stability.

Day 36–45: The roof was built using palm leaves layered tightly for natural waterproofing. Clay mixture was used to seal gaps and keep the interior cool.

Day 46–55: We added modern-style details — a bamboo staircase, balcony railing, and small window designs to let in sunlight and wind.

Day 56–65: The surroundings were landscaped with natural stone steps and a mini pool area for relaxation. A fireplace and bamboo chairs were added inside the house.

Day 66–69: The final touches — smoothing the clay walls, cleaning the floors, and decorating with local materials to complete the secret modern jungle treehouse.

This video captures the beauty of nature and hard work — a dream home hidden among the trees, built only with primitive tools and traditional knowledge. Every hammer, cut, and tie was done by hand with patience and passion.

snippet.title: 9 Survival Items the Amish Buy in Bulk — All Under $7 at Walmart
snippet.description:
🔗 The complete Amish Home System — every method from every video, room by room:
https://eliyodersecrets.com
https://youtu.be/WyYz6MmHgT0

You walk into Walmart on a Tuesday afternoon and you see a man in a black hat, suspenders, a beard with no mustache, pushing a cart loaded with the cheapest, most boring items in the entire store. Salt. Vinegar. Candles. String. Every single item costs less than seven dollars, and every single one of them could keep your family alive when the power grid fails, when the shelves go empty, or when the dollar in your pocket finally buys nothing at all.

This video walks through the nine items the Amish buy at Walmart every week — from plain iodized salt at one dollar and twelve cents, to white vinegar at three dollars and twenty cents, to a roll of cotton string at two dollars and seventy cents that becomes an emergency candle wick burning for six hours on cooking oil you already own. It also covers a technique documented in the 1887 edition of The Old Farmer's Almanac and used by Pennsylvania Dutch settler Hans Herr in 1719 — a method so simple it was erased from every modern survival guide, because cotton string cannot be patented and cooking oil cannot be sold as a survival kit for ninety-nine dollars.

I was paying four hundred and twelve dollars a month for heat last winter. The Amish family I visited paid nothing. Same temperature outside. Same square footage. Different knowledge. The average American household spends over six hundred dollars a year on cleaning products that a three-dollar jug of white vinegar replaces. The average American spends four hundred and seventy-five dollars a month on groceries. The Amish family I lived with that winter spent ninety-two. And they ate better. The difference is the list. The difference is nine items, under seven dollars each, and the skill to use them — passed down for three hundred years by people who never depended on the system that was busy forgetting.

This is not for people building a homestead from scratch. This is for a man who already owns a house — brand new subdivision or farmhouse built in 1948 — and is tired of the electric bill deciding whether his family eats that month. Everything I have pulled out of these communities — every item, every method, every technique from this channel — is gathered in one place: The Amish Home System. Link in the first pinned comment.

snippet.title: Why Microgrids Could Replace Traditional Power Grids
snippet.description:
Extreme weather, rising renewables, and aging infrastructure are exposing the limits of traditional power grids.
Microgrids are emerging as the next phase of the global energy transition  small, intelligent systems that generate, store, and manage electricity locally.

What Shift:
More than 750 million people still lack reliable power.
In 2025, wildfires in California cut electricity to 400,000 homes; a Texas blizzard left 4.5 million without supply.
As solar and wind expand, grid instability and curtailment are accelerating.

Why Microgrids Matter:
Operate independently during outages.
Enable renewable integration with local storage.
Provide backup for hospitals, airports, and industrial parks.
Deliver fast electrification to rural and island regions.

Global Developments:
United States: $10 billion invested through GRIP; Texas launches a $1.8 billion hospital and water-facility program.
Germany: the Pfinztal microgrid integrates wind, solar, and a 10 MWh flow battery for campus stability.
China: over 300 projects underway; Xuzhou Industrial Park system achieves 92 % renewable utilisation.
India: Kavaratti Island’s solar + storage hybrid ensures reliable power across the island.
Kenya: Wasini Island microgrid supplies 4,000 residents with 737 kW solar + 2.2 MWh storage.

Technology Core:
Distributed generation (solar, wind).
Energy storage for balancing supply and demand.
AI-based control systems for real-time forecasting and dispatch.

Policy and Market Drivers:
Inflation Reduction Act (US).
Renewable Energy Act and Climate Action Plan (Germany).
Microgrid Systems Act (Philippines).
ARENA regional funding (Australia).

Challenges Ahead:
High upfront costs and long payback.
Complex policy and interconnection rules.
Unclear revenue models for local trading.

Future Outlook:
Microgrids are evolving from emergency backup to core infrastructure.
With AI, long-duration storage, and virtual power plants, they are becoming the backbone of decentralized, resilient energy systems.

snippet.title: ⭐️ tastiest salad | meal prep |  4-5 days batch ⭐️
snippet.description:
Keep yours salads interesting & high protein with this ‘Mexican Salad’ Meal Prep ⭐️🤤 

Here’s your recipe 👇🌱 (makes 4 jars)

Ingredients:
- Rajma– 1.5 cups, boiled
- Paneer – 100 gm in cubes
- Sweet corn – 1.5 cup, boiled
- Olive oil – 2 tbsp
- Peri peri seasoning
- Smoked sea salt – to taste
- Curd (yogurt) – 1/2 cup
- Coriander – 2 tbsp, chopped
- Lime – 1 small
- Cucumber – 1 cup, chopped
- Tomatoes – 1 cup, chopped

Method:
1. Boil rajma, mash gently. Sauté in olive oil with peri peri and smoked sea salt. Add paneer cubes, splash of water, cook.
2. Boil sweet corn, air fry with peri peri, salt, and a little olive oil.
3. In a bowl, mix curd, chopped coriander, and lime juice.
4. Add chopped cucumber and tomatoes.
5. Fold in the rajma-paneer prep and crispy corn. Mix.
6. Divide into jars or enjoy right away 🙌
